message.content:
Below are two ways to launch a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Important**  
> * Google Cloud does **not** use the “EC2” terminology – that’s AWS.  
> * You must have the **Compute Engine API** enabled for your project and a valid OAuth token (or a service‑account key) that has `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` (and optionally `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser`).  
> * The GPU type `nvidia-a6000` is only available in certain zones (e.g., `us-central1-b`, `us-east1-c`, `asia-east1-a`, …). Check the [GPU availability page](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus#available_zones) for your region.

---

## 1. `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-b"          # pick a zone that supports A6000
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # adjust CPU/RAM as needed
DISK_SIZE_GB=100              # boot disk size
SERVICE_ACCOUNT="default"     # or a custom SA
NETWORK="default"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --boot-disk-size="${DISK_SIZE_GB}GB" \
  --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
  --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
  --accelerator="type=nvidia-a6000,count=1" \
  --service-account="$SERVICE_ACCOUNT" \
  --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" \
  --network="$NETWORK" \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root disk. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu Cloud image project. |
| `--accelerator` | Attaches one RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--service-account` | The SA that the VM will run as. |
| `--scopes` | Grants the VM full Cloud Platform access (adjust if you want tighter scopes). |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: runs a shell script at first boot (e.g., to install drivers). |
| `--tags` | Enables HTTP/HTTPS firewall rules if you plan to expose services. |

> **Tip:** If you need a *custom* machine type (e.g., 16 vCPUs, 64 GB RAM), use `--machine-type="custom-16-65536"`.

---

## 2. REST API Call (JSON)

If you prefer to use the raw REST API (e.g., from a script or a CI/CD pipeline), here’s the minimal JSON payload and the corresponding `curl` command.

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-b"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)   # or use a service‑account key

# JSON body
cat <<EOF > instance.json
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF

# POST request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

### Notes on the JSON payload

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `machineType` | Full URL to the machine type. |
| `disks[0].initializeParams.sourceImage` | Uses the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image family. |
| `guestAccelerators[0]` | Specifies the RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `networkInterfaces[0].network` | Connects to the default VPC. |
| `serviceAccounts[0].scopes` | Grants full Cloud Platform access. |
| `metadata.items[0]` | Optional startup script (here installing NVIDIA driver). |

> **Security Tip:** Store the OAuth token or service‑account key securely (e.g., in Secret Manager) and never hard‑code it in public repos.

---

## Quick Checklist

1. **Enable APIs**  
   ```bash
   gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com
   ```

2. **Verify GPU quota**  
   ```bash
   gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="zone:$ZONE" --format="table(name,available)"
   ```

3. **Create the instance** (using either method above).

4. **Verify GPU installation** (once the VM is running):  
   ```bash
   ssh $INSTANCE_NAME@external-ip
   nvidia-smi
   ```

That’s all you need to spin up a Compute Engine VM with an RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS!
